title: How the paper checks its fear scores
caption: These source-paper image pairs were shown to human annotators. In each original pair, the left image received a higher fear classification and the right image was a comparison; pair order was randomized for annotators. A model label should not be interpreted as proof of the person’s internal emotion.
alt: Six pairs of cable-news frames used in the paper’s human comparison of estimated fear expressions.
credit: Broadcast images from Fox News, CNN and MSNBC; reproduced from Ash and Caliskan’s research manuscript.

title: Comparing seven estimated expressions
caption: The original coefficient plots compare emotion classifications around opposing-party mentions. The joint and separate specifications both identify fear as the clearest positive relationship. Error bars show 95% confidence intervals; models account for the cable channel and detected word.
alt: Two original coefficient plots compare anger, disgust, happiness, fear, neutrality, sadness and surprise, with fear showing a positive association with opposing-party mentions.

title: Persistence, party and public topics
caption: The original parameter plot compares estimates for seven countries. Persistence in prior ties and same-party membership generally matter more than demographic similarity. The plotted intervals show the uncertainty reported in the manuscript; the networks represent shared hashtag use rather than direct conversations.
alt: An original interval plot compares intercept, age difference, prior-edge persistence, same-party and same-gender parameters across seven countries.

title: When ideological blocs move together or apart
caption: Six original panels compare the model’s within- and between-bloc attraction parameters. Positive values indicate modeled coalescence and negative values fragmentation over time, conditional on the network model. These estimates describe public discourse dynamics, not private bargaining or personal feelings.
alt: Six interval plots compare left–left, center–left, center–center, right–left, right–center and right–right attraction estimates across seven countries.

title: Street images and the depth model’s estimates
caption: Four source-paper examples pair images labeled Haifa, Jerusalem, Nazareth and Tel Aviv with outputs from the DepthAnything outdoor base model. The color fields are model-estimated depth, not ground-truth measurements.
alt: Four rows from the original paper compare urban street images with their colored predicted depth maps.
credit: Images and model outputs reproduced from the public research manuscript.

title: Comparing relative spacing across classified pairs
caption: The original YOLOv9e gender-merged specification plots normalized-distance estimates with 95% intervals. RA denotes the paper’s Religious Arab category, RJ Religious Jew, N Neutral, and NR Non-Religious. The red point shows the reference intercept; the other points show contrasts with that reference. Units are normalized, not meters.
alt: An original interval plot compares normalized-distance contrasts for ten pair categories, with same-group RA–RA and RJ–RJ contrasts below zero.
